name: Brightside Health
one_liner: Online psychiatry and therapy for depression and anxiety: video visits, messaging and medication, with insurance or self-pay.

short_description: Telehealth psychiatry and therapy for depression and anxiety, with monthly prescriber visits, weekly therapy sessions and symptom tracking; insurance.
long_description: Brightside Health is a US telehealth practice for people with depression, anxiety and related conditions. After an online assessment you can choose psychiatry (a monthly video visit with a prescriber plus messaging), therapy (weekly 45-minute video sessions plus messaging) or both, and you track your symptoms with regular questionnaires. It is in network with plans including Aetna, Cigna, Anthem and UnitedHealthcare and some Medicare and Medicaid plans; self-pay prices reported in October 2026 were $95 a month for psychiatry, $299 for therapy and $349 for both, with medication costs extra. Brightside's own researchers have published observational studies of its patients, including one with a non-randomized comparison group in which treated patients were more likely to see suicidal thoughts resolve. Clinical records are covered by its HIPAA notice, but its website privacy policy allows advertising partners to place tracking tools.
patient_summary: You complete an online assessment, then see a prescriber by video once a month, a therapist weekly, or both, and message your care team in between. You can use insurance (many plans are accepted) or pay about $95 a month for psychiatry or $299 a month for therapy. Medication is billed separately.

faqs.q: How much does Brightside Health cost?
faqs.a: With insurance, copays typically range from $0-60 per visit. Self-pay plans start around $95-200/month depending on services. Medication costs are separate and may be covered by insurance. The platform provides clear pricing upfront.

faqs.q: Does Brightside Health prescribe anxiety medication?
faqs.a: Yes, Brightside psychiatrists and psychiatric NPs prescribe medications for anxiety, depression, and related conditions. They focus on appropriate first-line treatments and avoid controlled substances as their primary focus. Your provider will recommend the best treatment approach.

faqs.q: Can I get therapy and medication through Brightside?
faqs.a: Yes, Brightside offers both psychiatry and therapy. Many patients benefit from combined treatment. You can receive medication management, therapy, or both based on your needs and clinician recommendations.

faqs.q: How does Brightside track treatment outcomes?
faqs.a: Brightside uses standardized assessments (PHQ-9, GAD-7) to track symptom improvement over time. This data helps clinicians adjust treatment. Patients can see their progress, and research shows outcome tracking improves results.
